label: Absolute Value
overview: Absolute value |x| gives the distance from zero, so it is always non-negative. SAT questions involve solving equations and inequalities with absolute value expressions. The key insight: |expression| = k splits into two cases — the expression equals +k or −k. Inequalities follow a similar split.

keyFormulas.name: No solution
keyFormulas.latex: |A| = k \text{ has no solution when } k < 0

commonMistakes.mistake: Splitting |A| = k into A = k only (forgetting the negative case)
commonMistakes.fix: Absolute value equations always produce two cases: A = k AND A = −k.

commonMistakes.mistake: Writing |A| < k as A < k without the lower bound
commonMistakes.fix: Less-than absolute value means a middle interval: −k < A < k (both bounds needed).

quickTip: Isolate the absolute value expression first before splitting into cases. If you get |A| = negative number, stop — there are no real solutions.
